If transparent huge pages are enabled
column2: we can isolate many more pages

column1: than we actually need to scan
column2: because we count both single and huge

column1: pages equally in isolate_lru_pages().
Since commit 5bc7b8aca942d (""mm: thp: add split tail pages to shrink
page list in page reclaim"")
column2: we scan all the tail pages immediately

column1: after a huge page split (see shrink_page_list()).  As a result
reclaim up to SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX * HPAGE_PMD_NR (512 MB) in one run!
This is easy to catch on memcg reclaim with zswap enabled.  The latter
makes swapout instant so that if we happen to scan an unreferenced huge
page we will evict both its head and tail pages immediately
likely to result in excessive reclaim.
